expectations.text: A PNG deliverable exists with its long side at least 2000 pixels (300-dpi render scale)
The image is wider than tall (PAE matrix panel rendered alongside the structure, aspect ratio > 1.3)
expectations.evidence: ratio=1.00 (programmatic). Viewed the PNG: the 2181x2181 square image contains ONLY the pLDDT-colored structure on a transparent background — no PAE panel was rendered alongside it, hence the 1:1 aspect.

expectations.text: The structure is colored by pLDDT confidence (blue-to-yellow/orange gradient over the chain), not by chain or rainbow position colors
expectations.evidence: Viewed the PNG: the single chain runs blue (helical core) through green to yellow/orange (terminal/loop regions) — the pLDDT ramp, matching `--color plddt` in commands.log.

expectations.text: A PAE matrix heat-map panel is visible in the image
expectations.evidence: Viewed the full PNG at native resolution: no heat-map panel appears anywhere in the image — only the structure canvas. The old export.py captures a single viewer element, so the PAE panel generated by `--pae` stayed in the viewer HTML and never reached the PNG.

expectations.text: interpretation.md exists and cites specific regions (residue numbers or domain/range descriptions) as high- vs low-confidence
interpretation.md identifies at least one low-confidence/disordered segment

notes: Root cause of both failures: the old export.py exports one viewer canvas, not the page — with `--pae` the heat-map panel exists in the HTML but is never captured into the PNG, and the square 700x700 view yields ratio 1.00. The runner also hit 404s on AlphaFold v4 file URLs and had to recover pLDDT/PAE data by probing the cached viewer.html; interpretation.md was still the richer of the two variants (3841 chars, specific segments).
